criteria.criterion: Use Google Search to locate Gemini API documentation (attempt and navigation)

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Google homepage with the Google logo and the search box active. In the search box, the typed query reads “Gemini API documentation”. An autocomplete dropdown is open showing suggestions such as “gemini api documentation”, “gemini api documentation python”, “gemini api documentation pdf”, “gemini api documentation javascript”, “gemini api documentation models”, “gemini api documentation java”, “gemini api documentation github”, “gemini api documentation nodejs”, “gemini api documentation download”, and “gemini api documentation mcp”. No search results page is shown and no documentation page is open.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Only the initial Google Search attempt (typing a query and seeing suggestions) is evidenced. The screenshot does not show submitting the search, seeing results, or opening an official Gemini API documentation page. So this criterion is not fully satisfied based on the screenshot (at best partial progress toward searching).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output mentions being blocked by a CAPTCHA/bot-detection page, but this screenshot shows the normal Google homepage with query suggestions—no CAPTCHA or “unusual traffic” message is visible here.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Google bot-detection page with a reCAPTCHA box labeled “I’m not a robot” and the reCAPTCHA logo. Below “About this page,” text reads: “Our systems have detected unusual traffic from your computer network. This page checks to see if it’s really you sending the requests, and not a robot.” There is also a “Why did this happen?” link. It does not show any Google Search results or any opened documentation page.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: No evidence in the screenshot that the agent successfully used Google Search results to locate and open Gemini API documentation. The screenshot instead shows search being blocked by a CAPTCHA, preventing navigation to results from what is visible.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims Google Search presented a CAPTCHA page before results; this matches what is visible. However, there is no evidence of proceeding via an alternative navigation path to official docs (only the CAPTCHA page is shown).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Google homepage (large multicolor “Google” logo), a central search box with microphone and Google Lens icons, and buttons “Google Search” and “I’m Feeling Lucky.” Top right shows “Gmail,” “Images,” an apps grid icon, and a blue “Sign in” button. No search results page is visible and no Gemini documentation page is open.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: From the screenshot alone, there is no evidence that Google Search results were reached or that any result was opened. It only shows the Google homepage ready for a query. Therefore the criterion (using Google Search to locate and open official Gemini API documentation) is not satisfied in the visible state.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output mentions a CAPTCHA/bot-detection page, but the screenshot does not show any CAPTCHA or “unusual traffic” message—only the normal Google homepage.

scoring.criterion: Use Google Search to locate Gemini API documentation (attempt and navigation)
scoring.justification: The agent dismissed cookies, entered the query “Gemini API documentation,” submitted the search, and upon encountering a CAPTCHA, clearly reported the issue. This constitutes a reasonable Google Search attempt despite the uncontrollable blocker.
scoring.applicable_evidence: Action History shows the agent used Google Search: dismissed consent, typed query "Gemini API documentation", then pressed Enter. Screenshot 4 (latest) confirms Google Search was blocked by an unusual-traffic reCAPTCHA on https://www.google.com/sorry/index before any results were shown. No screenshot shows search results or an opened documentation page.
scoring.post_image_justification: The agent made a reasonable attempt to use Google Search but was blocked by a CAPTCHA (an uncontrollable blocker). Under the principles, this still merits full credit for the attempt/navigation criterion even though it could not proceed to results.
scoring.reality_notes: Screenshots show the agent on the Google homepage, typing the query “Gemini API documentation” with autocomplete suggestions visible, but no submitted search results page is shown. A later screenshot shows a Google “unusual traffic” interstitial with a reCAPTCHA checkbox, indicating that attempting to access search results triggered a bot-detection block before any results or documentation page could be opened.

No screenshot shows search results or an opened documentation page.

So award partial credit for the demonstrated search attempt under a blocker, but not full credit for locating/opening docs.
scoring.reality_notes: DOM states show the Google homepage search UI with the query context visible (suggestions/history and a search box), and then a Google bot-detection interstitial stating unusual traffic and that a CAPTCHA must be solved to continue to the search results.
